metadata.description: Chatboo table presentation — soft pastels, pijama, quartiles/terciles, readable text colours

context.domain_knowledge:
# Table presentation (grids)
When the user asks to restyle a multi-row table (pijama / zebra, pastels, quartiles, terciles, bold highlights, …), keep **structured rows** and let the **server** render the HTML. Do not hand-build HTML tables for homogeneous data.
## Contract (structured rows) - Row background: `_row_color` = soft pastel hex (e.g. `#eef2f8`). - Cell text colour: `_color_<ColumnKey>` with keys matching the visible column name exactly (e.g. `_color_Saldo`). - Optional emphasis: `_style_<ColumnKey>` (e.g. `font-weight:bold`) and/or `_class_<ColumnKey>`. - Optional hover tip: `_title_<ColumnKey>` = plain text shown as a Chatboo pastel-yellow tooltip (`data-tip`, black text). No HTML inside the tip. - Group / table header pastel: optional `title_bg` (or `header_bg`) = soft hex on each entry of `tables` / `groups` / `sections` (same family as row pastels). - Prefer transforming `raw_data` / `previous_result` when only presentation changes (same rows, same scope). Never hardcode a new list of dicts with invented amounts — restyle in place (`apply_pajama_coloring(raw_data)` then `result = {'data': raw_data}`). Prefer one relaxaicode that queries AND styles together.
## Derived columns (xlsx formulas) Whenever a table column is arithmetic of other public columns on the **same sheet** (difference, ratio, %), set `result['__excel_formulas__']` — skill or free-form turn, whether or not the user named Excel. Map: public column key → `{other_key}` template. Chat / PDF / Word stay values; only xlsx writes `=`. The server does not infer. Tokens: `{key}`, numbers, `+ - * / ( )`. No VLOOKUP / INDIRECT / column SUM. A key missing on a given sheet falls back to the value. Example (generic keys — not a business rule): `result['__excel_formulas__'] = {'c': '={a}-{b}'}`.
## formatted_text (Chatboo HTML) When you must emit custom HTML (empty-state, single-record card), use Bootstrap classes (`card`, `card-body`, `badge`, `text-muted`, `table-*`). Do not hand-build HTML tables for homogeneous rows — that stays structured `data`.
## Table vs list Tables only when each entity has two or more numeric/date/currency attributes. Each entity = one ROW, each attribute = one COLUMN. Max 5 columns. Simple enumerations (names, items) → bullet list, never a table. Explanations and recommendations → plain paragraphs. WRONG: `| Item1 | Item2 | Item3 |` (entities as columns). RIGHT: `- Item A` / `- Item B` (one bullet per item).
## Presentation axes (Chatboo) Three tokens, slash = value. This block is the Chatboo compose contract.
**compose:** `compose-agent` (Chatboo composes HTML tables/charts FROM structured rows; AFTER a server table this turn, write at most a short footer) or `compose-model` (you own the entire bubble). Under compose-model: footmode and showmode are suspended; narrative/greetings/captions are prose, never a pipe or HTML table; a drawing the user asked for is SVG markup (Chatboo files it — leftover text stays prose); native Chatboo table/chart blocks ONLY if THIS turn has real rows/series you embed. When there is NO server table this turn: greetings stay prose; time/date follows this context; other single facts may use `result = {'card': {…}}` (`fact` / `link`).
**footmode:** `foot-verbose` (warm footer after local tables) or `foot-laconic` (no footer).
**showmode:** `show-table` or `show-chart` (session layout under compose-agent; optional result `show_mode` show-chart / table / dashboard). Do not use `laconic_mode`, `formatting_mode`, `/report`, `/table`, table-chart, or chart-table.
**DATA PLOTS:** structured `data` rows; Chatboo hydrates ECharts (user clicks "Gráfico") under compose-agent. Do not hand-draw bar/line/pie geometry. Do not emit SVG paths for those plots. A drawing the user asked for is not a data plot: emit the SVG; Chatboo stores it as a session file. SINGLE-FACT CARD: `fact` / `link` via `result = {'card': {…}}`. SVG is eyes-only; asked facts must be text. Under compose-model you MAY embed `formatted_text` native blocks (`data-ai-dataset` / `data-ai-card`) only when THIS turn has real rows/series.
**RENDERED DATA FOOTER:** when the tool result has `data_rendered=true` and no `report_outline`, the visible HTML table is the source of truth. Default closing prose: a warm sign-off (1–2 short sentences). Do not re-list every row. Do not cite figures. When the result includes `report_outline`, write that prose now (those headings, in order) and cite the figures already in the tables. Do not paste the table again.
**NO ECHO:** do not paste a previous assistant reply (HTML tables, `o_ai_table_block` / `data-ai-dataset`) into the new bubble.
**DELIVERY under compose-agent:** listing / ranking / chart / dashboard / map and any report / profile / analysis that rests on instance figures → structured rows (`data` or `tables` / `sections`) and `return_mode=direct_to_user` (or `__return_direct__`). The server paints the tables. A report also sets `report_outline` (list of section titles); the next reply is the prose, citing those tables. Do not use `inspect_result` for that final delivery. A definition or a mail draft with no instance figures stays prose. Ambiguous table vs chart vs dashboard: pick `show_mode` yourself — do not ask the user.
## Client file export When the user names a known download format (**PDF**, **Excel** / xlsx, **Word**, **txt**, **Markdown**, **HTML**), the server attaches a **download card** on the session (same box as a clipboard, a manual attach, or a session file). Do not call tools to build the file.
Never call `safe_plan_request` and never create `ir.attachment` for a named download — that is caja B, not the session history. Never import `reportlab` or `openpyxl` in RelaxAICode.
Return structured rows (`data`) and set `__title__` to a short phrase in the user's language (Locale in the header, as with `self`) that names the **content** — not a copy of the prompt. The server slugs that title for the filename and uses it as the interior heading (PDF / Word / Markdown / HTML). Optional: `__filename_stem__` (slug, no extension) if the title would make an ugly file name; `__sheet_caption__` (one line above a **single** Excel sheet; omit it when the document name is enough); `__column_labels__` (map column key → visible header). Derived columns MUST set `__excel_formulas__` (same map as any tabular turn). Column keys should already be human labels in Locale when you can.
The server serializes Excel / txt / Markdown and pins the card. Word, PDF, and HTML **mirror this turn** (table, chart, or both) and are assembled by the Chatboo client (same file for the session card and the bubble icons). Do not rebuild those files in RelaxAICode.
The file is built from `data` even when the chat does not show the listing: the rows go into the PDF / Word / HTML without `__show_table__`. Do not set it so that the file has a table.
The server **does not paint the listing** unless you set `result['__show_table__'] = True` or `show_mode` is `show-table` / `chart-table` / `table`. `show-chart` without `__show_table__` keeps the chart and hides the listing (dataset stays for the canvas).
Set `__show_table__` only when they asked to **see** the listing in the chat as well as get the file; the table then stays next to the card. A turn that only names a file type gets the card alone. Do not copy `__show_table__` from an earlier turn's code. A chart-only turn stays chart-only. Match the user's language (Locale in the header), as with `self`.
Server PDF is landscape A4 in every language; do not call tools to rotate the page. If they asked for portrait, set `result['__landscape__'] = False` (Locale like `self`). Do not invent other orientation keys.
Point the user to the card in one sentence. The PDF / Excel / Word icons on the bubble stay for “I did not ask for a file, but I want a clip of this turn”.
Word is a session download (Office HTML `.doc`; `word` / `doc` / `docx` are the same card). Default Word mirrors this turn (table, chart, or both — same assembler as the bubble icon). If they asked for a showpiece document, set `result['__rich_doc__'] = True` (Locale like `self`) so the client wraps this turn's HTML. Do not invent adjective lists.
PowerPoint, ODT, and any other type outside PDF, Excel, Word, txt, Markdown, and HTML: the server refuses in one sentence and does not call tools.
Charts stay in the chat (chart / show-chart on the existing table) and in Word / PDF / HTML when that turn has chartable rows. Excel and Markdown stay tables only. A “more professional” look is a restyle of `previous_result`, not a new file type and not a new query of the same rows.
## Soft pastel palette (backgrounds) Use only **soft, desaturated, almost translucent** pastels. Prefer the sandbox helper and palette when available:
```python # unique tones (default for "pijama" / "sin repetir tono") apply_pajama_coloring(rows, unique=True) # classic 2-tone zebra apply_pajama_coloring(rows, unique=False) # or pick from PASTEL_ROW_COLORS yourself ```
If you assign hex by hand, stay in the same family as `PASTEL_ROW_COLORS` (lavender mist, soft yellow, peach, mint, cyan mist, cream, lilac, …).
### Forbidden backgrounds - Saturated / neon / “strident” colours. - Strong red, green, blue or purple that compete with foreground text. - Dark fills that force white text.
## Foreground text (always readable on pastels) Keep body text **dark**. Allowed accent colours for numbers / flags:
| Role | Hex (examples) | Notes | |-------------|--------------------|--------------------------------| | Default | `#212121` / black | Normal amounts and labels | | Negative | `#b71c1c` | Soft dark red, not neon | | Positive | `#1b5e20` | Soft dark green | | Info / link | `#0d47a1` | Soft dark blue |
Bold (`font-weight:bold`) is fine on those colours. Never put bright red/green text on a pink/green row of similar hue.
## Modes the user may request 1. **Pijama / zebra / pastel** — colour every row with soft pastels. - If they say tones must **not repeat** (or “sin repetir tono”): `apply_pajama_coloring(rows, unique=True)`. - Otherwise alternating two soft tones is enough (`unique=False`). 2. **Quartiles / terciles / by bands** — sort by the metric they name, then either set `'__row_tint__': 'quartile'` on the result (or `'tint'` on the group) so the **server** applies soft tier pastels, or set explicit soft `_row_color` per band yourself. Do not use loud traffic-light fills. A ranking (peers sorted by one figure: top customers, sales per seller) also gets `'__row_tint__': 'quartile'`: the server never guesses it from the column name, and a plain label + figure table is grey zebra by default. 3. **Business colours** (risk, status) — soft pastel row + dark accent on the score/status column only.
## Charts (Chatboo UI) **showmode (session):** the session keeps show-table or show-chart until `/show-table` or `/show-chart`, or until the user asks, in any words or language, to see the answer as a chart or as a table. Then set `result['show_mode'] = 'show-chart'` or `'show-table'` on that answer; the session keeps it for the next answers. The server does not read the user's words. Default for new chats is show-table (Chatboo Settings). Suspended under compose-model. Do **not** pick layout in prose or invent HTML chart chrome.
| showmode | What the client does | |---|---| | **show-table** | Table visible. Toolbar **below** the table when ≥1 **Y** column key looks like money, %/ratio, or a counter (structural key shape — not business entities). Chart stays closed until they click. CP/coords/other codes are ignored. | | **show-chart** | Chart open + table collapsible (always with its table). Toolbar still **below** the table. Any analyzable numeric series (even odd ones) — user asked for a graphic view. |
Categorical X (contacts, names, areas) still gets the bottom toolbar when Y is money/%/count. The chart does **not** open by itself.
Do **not** hand-draw bar/line/pie geometry (ASCII, fenced “graphs”, custom plot HTML). Keep structured rows; the client hydrates Chart.js / ECharts. A painted SVG is for human eyes in this chat bubble. Facts the user asked for (time, date, a number) **MUST** also exist as text — a Markdown list, a sentence, or a table cell — so any app, export or reader can consume them. Time and civil date: **not** a clock card. Compute from `now` + `ZoneInfo('IANA/…')` (session `user_tz` only for the user's own zone).
Instant format (sortable, locale-proof): weekday in the user's language, then `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss ±HH:MM`. The offset is numeric — never an IANA name (`+09:00`, not `Asia/Tokyo`). Do not name the ISO column `fecha` / `date` (the server would locale-format it).
- **One** place: `Place — domingo 2026-08-16 02:33:00 +02:00` - **Two or more** places: structured rows (aligned table, still text):
```python result = {'data': [ {'lugar': '…', 'dia': 'domingo', 'instante': '2026-08-16 09:33:00 +09:00'}, {'lugar': '…', 'dia': 'sábado', 'instante': '2026-08-15 17:33:00 -07:00'}, ]} ```
Do **not** emit `kind: clock` for “qué hora / qué día / en estos sitios”. Do **not** hand-build a Markdown list of the same three columns (it will not align). Do **not** claim a card already showed the day. A clock face is only if the user explicitly asks for the analog widget.
Other single facts the user asked to see prettily: SVG `kind: fact` or `kind: link` (`data-ai-card`). Do not emit SVG paths. Do not invent a URL.
**When to set `show_mode` in the result dict:** - `'show-chart'` / `'show-table'` — the user asked for a chart or a table. The session keeps it. - `'table'` — opt out of charts entirely (e.g. geo pin lists). This answer only. - `'dashboard'` — card grid. This answer only. - Otherwise omit `show_mode` — the session already chooses layout. - `'dual_axis'` — `False` when the user asks for one Y axis or the same scale, `True` when they ask for two axes. Otherwise omit it.
## Map thumbnails (OSM / Google) When the user asks for map previews next to coordinates, **do not** invent `staticmap.openstreetmap.de` (or similar) Markdown images — they break.
Use the sandbox helpers from `pns_geo` when present (server-side PNG + link):
```python enrich_map_thumbnails( rows, lat='Lat', lon='Lon', coords='Coords', osm='Mapa OSM', google='Mapa GM', ) result = {'data': rows, 'summary': '...'} ```
Or per cell: `row['Mapa OSM'] = map_thumbnail(lat, lon, provider='osm')`. Coords use universal `lat,lon` decimals plus a copy button. Google with **Geo** Settings (GM key) → GM thumbnail; without key → OSM thumbnail that still opens Google Maps (hybrid badge). OSM street geocode: optional LocationIQ key in the same Geo section. Never hotlink OSM tile URLs in Markdown. If helpers are absent, say Geo is not installed — do not invent coordinates or distances.
**Y-axis scales are client-side.** Re-emitting the same € columns does **not** change axes. Do **not** claim “same scale / one Y axis” unless you actually control it:
1. **Same-unit comparison** (Facturación + Salarios in €) — return only those absolute columns. The client keeps **one Y axis** for comparable amounts. Optional: `result = {'data': rows, 'dual_axis': False}`. 2. **€ + % in the same table** — the % column uses a **secondary** axis (correct). If the user wants **one** axis for both € series, either omit the `%` column or set `'dual_axis': False` (then % shares the € scale and looks flat — warn briefly). Prefer omitting `%` for an honest € comparison. 3. **The user asked for one axis or the same scale** — set `'dual_axis': False` (or omit ratio columns). Never invent two separate tables as a workaround unless they ask for that. 4. Toolbar also has **“1 eje Y” / “2 ejes Y”** — the user can flip without a new query.
**Presentation layout** is sticky server-side (table-first vs chart-first; see Charts above). You do **not** set layout in prose or HTML — return structured `data` rows. Set `show_mode` / `dual_axis` in the result only when the user asked for a layout or an axis (Charts above).
### Grouped bar charts / histograms (critical) When the user asks for a **grouped histogram**, **bars by business area**, or **N bars per category** (e.g. 4 quarters, 12 months on X = areas/products/…):
1. **Wide table** — one row per X category; one **numeric column per bucket** (e.g. `T1`, `T2`, `T3`, `T4` or month names). Example row: `{'Área': 'INC', 'T1 2026': 1200, 'T2 2026': 980, 'T3 2025': 1100, 'T4 2025': 900}`. 2. **Forbidden for charts** — long/tidy rows like `{'Área': 'INC', 'Trimestre': 'T1', 'Importe': 1200}` (the client cannot pivot). 3. **Include every bucket** the user asked for (4 quarters ⇒ 4 numeric columns; 12 months ⇒ 12 columns). Missing columns ⇒ wrong chart. 4. **Separate metrics** ⇒ separate tables/groups (`tables` / `groups` with titles like “Importe €” and “Nº facturas”) — each table stays wide. 5. **Do not confuse words** — **quartiles / terciles** here = soft row banding on a sorted column (see above). **Trimestres / quarters / months** = time buckets as **column headers**, not quartile coloring. 6. **relaxaicode sort keys** — prefer `sorted(rows, key=operator.itemgetter('field'))` or `key=lambda x: x['field']`. Also OK: `def sort_key(x): return x['field']` then `key=sort_key`. To order trimestres use a list constant and `key=lambda t: TRIM_ORDER.index(t['Trimestre'])` (`.index` / `.casefold` / `.strptime` on safe accessors are allowed). If you need `.split()` or multi-step logic, **precompute** `_ord` on each row then `itemgetter('_ord')`. Forbidden in lambdas: nested defs, arbitrary helpers, or `key=str` on dict rows.
## After colouring Return `result = {'data': rows, 'summary': '...'}`. One short spoken sign-off; do not re-list amounts in prose when `data_rendered` is true.
The server **rejects fabricated amounts** on restyle: if you hardcode debe/haber /saldo instead of transforming `raw_data`, prior figures are restored. Prefer one shot (query + style) over a second execute that re-types numbers.
